children: The Indian rupee is set to resume its rally on Wednesday, supported by a revival in foreign investor appetite for local equities and a mounting sense that the currency's outlook is turning more favourable.

The rupee  is expected to open at 92.70-92.75 to the dollar, according to traders, after dipping from a seven-month high of 92.43 to settle at 92.91 on Monday. Indian financial markets were shut on Tuesday for a holiday.
Monday marked a pause in the rupee's recent rally, with heavy corporate dollar buying and technical indicators suggesting the currency had become significantly overbought, prompting a pullback.
Most bankers, however, viewed the retreat as a healthy correction after a recent run-up, rather than a reversal in the currency's upward momentum.
"For now, the move from 92.50 to 93 looks little more than a routine correction following the big dip (on dollar/rupee)," a currency trader at a bank said.

"The underlying picture remains favourable (for the rupee). It probably requires a major flare-up in oil prices or a reversal in foreign investor flows to bring back the old trade (of selling the rupee on rallies)."
A turnaround in foreign investor sentiment towards India is becoming increasingly evident, with overseas funds buying local equities on Monday despite a nearly 2% drop in benchmark indexes.
Foreign investors have poured more than $14 billion into Indian equities so far this month, helping lift the rupee by more than 2%.
This shift in sentiment comes against the backdrop of mounting  concerns over AI valuations and the sustainability of the technology-led rally, which is prompting investors to reassess allocations.
The AI trade remains a key variable for the rupee, with bankers saying swings in technology shares will decide the direction of foreign flows into Indian assets.
The Nasdaq has seen significant volatility sessions amid heightened sensitivity to Nvidia-related developments and the broader question over the returns on AI investments.
